18	  - "DO NOT BUILD FROM SOURCE. Directus publishes directus/directus and the repo is a large monorepo. Pin the major (directus/directus:12 was current 2026-08-16) rather than :latest, so a redeploy cannot cross a major version and run a migration the user did not ask for."
19	  - "⛔ SET SECRET EXPLICITLY AND KEEP IT. It signs the access tokens. Left unset, Directus generates one per boot, which means a redeploy silently logs out every user and breaks any integration holding a token."
20	  - "DATABASE: Directus does not read DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/DATABASE_URL to the project .env, so remap by hand onto Directus's names: DB_CLIENT=pg, DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", DB_DATABASE=\"${PGDATABASE}\", DB_USER=\"${PGUSER}\", DB_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". Managed-DB defaults are database `app` and user `appuser`, so DB_DATABASE ends up `app`, which is fine."
21	  - "⛔ PERSIST /directus/uploads OR THE FILE LIBRARY IS A LIE. Directus stores uploaded files on local disk by default, and the database only holds the metadata rows. Without a volume on that path a redeploy leaves a file library full of entries whose files are gone: the UI lists them, every one 404s, and nothing warns you. Mount a named volume on /directus/uploads. Mount one on /directus/extensions too if the user will install extensions."
22	  - "ADMIN ACCOUNT: ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD create the first admin on the FIRST boot only, against an empty database. Generate the value, pass it at deploy time, hand it to the user, and do not commit it."
23	  - "PORT 8055, which is not a port anyone guesses. Pass 8055 to deploy_compose; the health probe and the public hostname both hang off it."
24	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Directus bootstraps its own schema against an empty database on first boot, and runs its migrations on every start after that. The first boot against a fresh managed Postgres is noticeably slower than later ones; that is the bootstrap, not a hang."
25	  - "PUBLIC_URL should be the full https URL on the generated hostname. It is what Directus puts in emails and in OAuth redirects, and it defaults to a relative path, so leaving it unset produces links that work in the browser and break everywhere else. Generate the dname yourself in the full `directus-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
26	  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY, so password resets and invite emails do not work. If the user needs them, wire EMAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp and the EMAIL_SMTP_* family to a provider they own. Otherwise say plainly that the admin password is the only way in."
27	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 8055."
28	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, so there is no repo to point deploy_compose at. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Directus GitHub URL would make redu try to build the monorepo."
29	  - "LICENCE: Directus is under the Monospace Sustainable Core License 1.0. Its permitted purposes explicitly include deploying or hosting the software for a licensee, and internal use, so this deploy is squarely inside it. What is NOT permitted is a Competing Use, meaning redu offering Directus as its own paid managed service. Do not help anyone circumvent the licence-key functionality either; that is the one stated Limitation."
30	  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so content is not lost by accident, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely the user must also delete_database. Note the uploads volume goes with the app VM, so the files and the metadata are on different lifecycles."
31	---
32	
33	# Self-host Directus on redu
34	
35	An instant REST and GraphQL API over your own SQL database, with an admin app on top: one
36	container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your content and your files stay on
37	infrastructure you control, in the EU.
38	
39	## What this deploys
40	
41	- **Directus** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 8055.
42	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your content survives every redeploy.
43	- A volume for `/directus/uploads`, so your files do too.
44	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
45	
46	About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.
47	
48	## Deploy
49	
50	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
51	directory containing this file:
52	
53	    Read redu.md and deploy Directus on redu.
54	
55	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
56	
57	## The three that actually break it
58	
59	**Their compose file.** The `docker-compose.yml` in the Directus repo is labelled, in the file
60	itself, as debugging only. It brings up every database vendor they support and does not contain
61	the app. Write a one-service compose instead.
62	
63	**The uploads volume.** Directus keeps uploaded files on local disk and only the metadata in the
64	database. Redeploy without a volume on `/directus/uploads` and the file library still lists
65	every file, and every one of them 404s.
66	
67	**The secret.** Set `SECRET` yourself and keep it. Unset, Directus makes a new one each boot, so
68	every redeploy logs out every user and invalidates every issued token.
69	
70	## Licence, since it is a fair question
71	
72	Directus is under the Monospace Sustainable Core License 1.0. It permits internal use, and its
73	permitted purposes explicitly name deploying or hosting the software for a licensee. You deploy
74	it into your own account and you operate it, which is exactly that. What the licence stops is
75	someone offering Directus itself as a competing paid service.
76	
77	## Deploy log

# Self-host Directus on redu

An instant REST and GraphQL API over your own SQL database, with an admin app on top: one
container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your content and your files stay on
infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Directus** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 8055.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your content survives every redeploy.
- A volume for `/directus/uploads`, so your files do too.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Directus on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Their compose file.** The `docker-compose.yml` in the Directus repo is labelled, in the file
itself, as debugging only. It brings up every database vendor they support and does not contain
the app. Write a one-service compose instead.

**The uploads volume.** Directus keeps uploaded files on local disk and only the metadata in the
database. Redeploy without a volume on `/directus/uploads` and the file library still lists
every file, and every one of them 404s.

**The secret.** Set `SECRET` yourself and keep it. Unset, Directus makes a new one each boot, so
every redeploy logs out every user and invalidates every issued token.

## Licence, since it is a fair question

Directus is under the Monospace Sustainable Core License 1.0. It permits internal use, and its
permitted purposes explicitly name deploying or hosting the software for a licensee. You deploy
it into your own account and you operate it, which is exactly that. What the licence stops is
someone offering Directus itself as a competing paid service.

# Self-host Directus on redu

An instant REST and GraphQL API over your own SQL database, with an admin app on top: one
container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your content and your files stay on
infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Directus** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 8055.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your content survives every redeploy.
- A volume for `/directus/uploads`, so your files do too.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Directus on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Their compose file.** The `docker-compose.yml` in the Directus repo is labelled, in the file
itself, as debugging only. It brings up every database vendor they support and does not contain
the app. Write a one-service compose instead.

**The uploads volume.** Directus keeps uploaded files on local disk and only the metadata in the
database. Redeploy without a volume on `/directus/uploads` and the file library still lists
every file, and every one of them 404s.

**The secret.** Set `SECRET` yourself and keep it. Unset, Directus makes a new one each boot, so
every redeploy logs out every user and invalidates every issued token.

## Licence, since it is a fair question

Directus is under the Monospace Sustainable Core License 1.0. It permits internal use, and its
permitted purposes explicitly name deploying or hosting the software for a licensee, and internal use, so this deploy is squarely inside it.

# Self-host Directus on redu

An instant REST and GraphQL API over your own SQL database, with an admin app on top: one
container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your content and your files stay on
infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Directus** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 8055.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your content survives every redeploy.
- A volume for `/directus/uploads`, so your files do too.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Directus on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

**Their compose file.** The `docker-compose.yml` in the Directus repo is labelled, in the file
itself, as debugging only. It brings up every database vendor they support and does not contain
the app. Write a one-service compose instead.

database. Redeploy without a volume on `/directus/uploads` and the file library still lists
every file, and every one of them 404s.

every redeploy logs out every user and invalidates every issued token.

# Self-host Directus on redu

An instant REST and GraphQL API over your own SQL database, with an admin app on top: one
container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your content and your files stay on
infrastructure you control, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Directus** from the official image, on one m1.medium VM, port 8055.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your content survives every redeploy.
- A volume for `/directus/uploads`, so your files do too.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Directus on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**Their compose file.** The `docker-compose.yml` in the Directus repo is labelled, in the file
itself, as debugging only. It brings up every database vendor they support and does not contain
the app. Write a one-service compose instead.

**The uploads volume.** Directus keeps uploaded files on local disk and only the metadata in the
database. Redeploy without a volume on `/directus/uploads` and the file library still lists
every file, and every one of them 404s.

**The secret.** Set `SECRET` yourself and keep it. Unset, Directus makes a new one each boot, so
every redeploy logs out every user and invalidates every issued token.

## The one that wastes your time rather than breaking it

**`/server/health` is 403 unauthenticated.** Poll it from outside to decide whether the deploy is
up and it never answers, so a healthy Directus looks like a hang. Poll `/admin/login` instead, or
send an admin token.

## Licence, since it is a fair question

Directus is under the Monospace Sustainable Core License 1.0. It permits internal use, and its
permitted purposes explicitly name deploying or hosting the software for a licensee. You deploy
it into your own account and you operate it, which is exactly that. What the licence stops is
someone offering Directus itself as a competing paid service.
